items.summary: Anaxia, the BLLM engine, with the source, the Lean development and the checks of the paper BLLM: Beyond the LLM with Deep Human-Mind-AI by D. Bhattacharjee and U. Bhattacharya. The engine is the Python package eBLLM (command anaxia ), a Lean 4 library and the container image ghcr.io/creelie/bllm-engine, which carries no model weights. The paper proves, in a model with independent runs, that certifying self-modifications costs an entropy (the entropy law), that a sound infinite self-improvement of finite cost exists exactly when one series converges, that a proposer needs a number of proposals set by a Rényi entropy of order one half, and that n verified layers sharing one budget cost at least n log(n/θ). Sixty-five of its theorems are proved in Lean 4 with Mathlib, each depending only on the three standard axioms. The engine combines known constructions in a typed crossing network with a program check and a refuter for every candidate, a shared memory and five target agents, and builds new objects in construction mode: a goal-directed builder and an exists-forall search, each followed by an independent gate. From the rules of Steinberg's problem it rebuilds the gadgets of the 2016 counterexample of Cohen-Addad, Hebdige, Král', Li and Salgado; it finds nothing on Erdős's question for cycles of length 4 to 6. Layer towers of depth one to three, a ladder and a mesh, are compared with the crossing loop at the same number of checks. A Hodge-only run of twelve rounds leaves every target point at the same gap. None of the five benchmark problems (the lattice Yang–Mills mass gap, the Hodge conjecture, the standard conjecture of Lefschetz type, Chowla's conjecture, Erdős problem 1183) is solved. The registry of the systems, methods and collections the engine draws on, with what it takes from each and what it leaves, is src/ebllm/bllm/data/sources.json and Appendix D of the paper.

Its central proposition is deliberately testable: a swarm may change its topology after losing modules, but it earns the stronger name of functional regeneration only when its restored configuration satisfies the original, independently assessed service requirements and does not conceal emerging hazards or latent joint failures. The monograph distinguishes three often conflated networks: mechanical connections that transmit forces, communication links that transmit information, and power connections that transport energy. It then investigates how graph connectivity, geometric rigidity, elastic stiffness, buckling, frictional contact, thermal dissipation, material fatigue, sensing uncertainty, local negotiation, and safe rollback constrain what an apparently repaired swarm can actually do. A prospective twenty-module testbed provides recurring engineering anchors: bridge, gripping, and sensing-tower tasks, blinded removal of modules, unseen configurations, independent qualification, and strong comparisons with redundant fixed structures and specialist replacement procedures. items.summary: How much classical information can a noisy optical channel carry when both signal energy and preshared entanglement are limited? This work gives an exact capacity frontier for this joint resource problem. It allows one to determine the best asymptotic communication rate, price the benefit of additional entanglement, and distinguish the effect of tolerating errors from that of changing how entanglement is supplied. Exact capacity under two resource constraints The setting is any fixed bosonic Gaussian channel \(\Phi\) with finitely many input and output modes. Signal energy is measured by a positive quadratic Hamiltonian \(H_G=\tfrac12 R^{\mathsf T}GR\), with \(G>0\) and ground energy \(E_0\); \(R\) collects the canonical quadratures. The budgets satisfy \(E\ge E_0\) and \(P\ge0\). For an \(n\)-use code, the mean total signal energy is at most \(nE\), while the same initially shared maximally entangled state has Schmidt rank \(K_n\) satisfying \(\log K_n\le nP\). Thus \(P\) is a strictly supplied entanglement rate. Encoders may be arbitrary joint quantum operations, and decoding may be collective. The classical capacity is \[ C(E,P)=\max_{\substack{U\ge V\;\mathrm{physical}\\ \frac12\operatorname{Tr}(GU)\le E,\;S_G(V)\le P}}\bigl[S_G(\Phi U)+S_G(V)-S_G(\Phi^c V)\bigr]. \] Here \(V\) is a Gaussian seed covariance, \(U\) is the average-input covariance, and \(U-V\) is the displacement-modulation covariance. A covariance is physical when \(V+i\Omega/2\ge0\), where \(\Omega\) is the canonical commutation matrix and the vacuum covariance is \(I/2\). The notation \(S_G\) denotes Gaussian von Neumann entropy, and \(\Phi^c\) is the full complementary channel, including any environment purification. All logarithms are natural, so rates are in nats per channel use. This formula replaces optimization over arbitrary quantum block codes by a finite-dimensional covariance optimization. It supplies both an achievable rate and a converse against non-Gaussian, correlated encodings. At \(P=0\), it also determines the unassisted capacity of general fixed finite-mode Gaussian channels, including channels without a passive decomposition into independent modes. The reduction specifies the exact capacity value; it does not require a closed-form optimizer for every device. Energy and strict entanglement supply respond differently to errors For a fixed allowed average error \(0\le\varepsilon<1\), the exact capacity under the mean-energy constraint is \[ C_\varepsilon(E,P)=C\!\left(E_0+\frac{E-E_0}{1-\varepsilon},\,P\right). \] Allowing failure rescales the mean energy above the ground state, but leaves the strict initial entanglement budget unchanged. The proof uses an exponential strong converse for codes whose inputs obey a hard total-energy cutoff. In a different model, where a readable flag permits random entanglement supply constrained only on average, the work establishes an achievable bound and a strict small-supply advantage for thermal attenuation at positive energy and fixed nonzero error. That comparison identifies the operational importance of the supply rule; it is not a complete capacity characterization of the flagged model. The communication value of entanglement For a thermal attenuator, let \(0<\eta<1\) be the transmissivity, \(b>0\) the output mean photon number for vacuum input, and \(N\) the input mean photon number. Write its capacity as \(C_N(P)\), and define \(g(N)=(N+1)\log(N+1)-N\log N\). The gain from entanglement obeys the sharp bound \[ 0\le C_N(P)-C_N(0)\le\frac{\eta}{1+b}\,P. \] For every fixed \(N>0\), the coefficient \(\eta/(1+b)\) is attained as the initial right derivative at \(P=0\). In the low-photon limit, the stronger resource law is \[ C_N(P)-C_N(0)=\frac{\eta}{1+b}\min\{P,g(N)\}+O(N),\qquad N\downarrow0. \] The remainder is uniform over \(P\ge0\) at fixed \(\eta\) and positive \(b\). Noise therefore determines the conversion efficiency, while \(g(N)\sim N\log(1/N)\) sets the entanglement scale

items.summary: Devilray is a reconfigurable adversarial baseline designed to systematically explore realistic fake base station (FBS) behaviors and diagnose blind spots in existing and future detectors. Empirically anchored in the first academic analysis of a commercial FBS (C-FBS), Devilray establishes a unified four-phase pipeline and seven fundamental operational feature dimensions, systematically extending them via 3GPP specification-permitted variants. Through a modular, reconfigurable implementation, Devilray supports configuring diverse FBS instances by combining these variants across the pipeline. To govern this combinatorial operational space, Devilray incorporates a semantics-aware, rule-based dependency checker that prunes standard violations and empirically ineffective operations, defining a logically explorable space of 2,592 attack instances. Using Devilray, we evaluated seven accessible FBS detectors and surfaced adversarial blind spots rooted in assumption-bound designs. This artifact submission provides the complete Devilray source code, installation and execution guides, dependency-checker test configurations, an example FBS instance profile, all ten FBS instance profiles used in the paper, packet captures from these ten instances, and derived datasets for FBSDetector. These components support the Devilray implementation and dependency checker described in Sections 5.3 and 5.4, as well as the evaluations reported in Sections 6.1 and 8. Evaluators can install and build Devilray, execute the dependency-checker verification suite, launch Devilray using the provided configuration profiles, and rerun the FBSDetector evaluation on the included PCAP and CSV datasets. The artifact was validated on Ubuntu 22.04 and depends primarily on srsRAN 4G and LTESniffer. Executing Devilray over the air additionally requires an SDR and an isolated test environment. Also, note that conducting such experiments with UEs connected to commercial networks without appropriate safeguards may raise ethical and regulatory concerns. As described in the paper, our experiments employed a Faraday cage and repeater-based setup to prevent interference with commercial networks. Evaluators without either suitable SDR hardware or the safeguards required for over-the-air experiments can still build the complete software, exercise the dependency checker, and run the dataset-based FBSDetector evaluation. The primary goal of this artifact evaluation is to verify the availability of the source code and its basic functionality.
items.title: Devilray: A Reconfigurable Adversarial Baseline for Revealing Blind Spots in Fake Base Station Detection

items.summary: In autonomous driving, perceiving surrounding objects is not enough: failing to understand how they move and interact over time can lead to dangerous decisions. Evaluating vision-language models (VLMs) therefore requires testing whether they connect past spatial observations to future consequences. Yet existing benchmarks often assess edge cases through basic perception questions or test temporal understanding in simple scenarios, leaving complex spatiotemporal reasoning underexplored. We introduce STRIDE (SpatioTemporal Reasoning In Driving Edge Cases), an object-centric benchmark for long-tail, safety-critical driving scenarios. STRIDE covers six task families: spatial perception, spatial understanding, temporal memory, temporal extrapolation, trajectory prediction, and scene-context awareness. It pairs multiple-choice questions probing individual spatiotemporal judgments with related free-form visual question answering (VQA) requiring detailed scene explanations and justifications of driving decisions. We prioritize scenes with unusual object behaviors and complex traffic interactions, generate reference answers from structured dataset annotations through automated procedures, and use limited language-model assistance and human verification to ensure annotation quality. Across 12 proprietary, open-weight, and driving-specialized models, even the best performer, GPT-6-Astra, achieves only 43.4% average multiple-choice accuracy, versus an approximately 20% random-choice baseline. Further analysis reveals that strong performance in describing driving scenes does not necessarily translate to accurate safety-critical judgments, and that models struggle more with reconstructing object motion than recalling past positions. STRIDE thus exposes spatiotemporal driving limitations that aggregate VQA scores can conceal.
items.title: STRIDE: Evaluating Spatiotemporal Reasoning in Driving Edge Cases

items.summary: Code, independent checks and the record of the Anaxia engine for the paper Which String Vibrations Become Which Generations on the Dwork Quintic by Deep Bhattacharjee and Ushashi Bhattacharya. The paper determines, for the heterotic string with the standard embedding on the one-parameter family of quintic threefolds, which vibration modes become which families of charged particles. The 101 families are labelled by 101 distinct characters of the symmetry group (Z/5)^3, and the 24 characters that do not occur are the classes of the permutations of (0,1,2,3,4). Every Yukawa coupling allowed by the symmetry is a power of the modulus, psi^r with r = 0, 1, 2, 3 on 566, 425, 280 and 160 unordered triples, and every other coupling vanishes. The invariant deformation pairs each family with exactly one partner, so that the mass matrix has determinant psi^70, full rank away from the Fermat point and rank 51 there, where the masses are given in closed form by the Gamma function. The Geometric Selection Conjecture is shown to be equivalent to the existence of one viable vacuum fixed by mirror symmetry, and no smooth quintic and no free quotient of one carries three families. The existence of a viable vacuum is open. The archive holds 64 independent checks: a C program for the labels, the couplings allowed by the group and the mass map, a C++ expansion of the Hessian over its 120 permutations, Python checks of the socle, the Hessian, the intersection form of the Fermat quintic and the Gamma values, a Julia check of the Hodge norms, a Macaulay2 computation of the Jacobian ring at two rational values of the modulus with the socle functional on all 3876 monomials of degree fifteen, and 11 Lean 4 theorems on the counts and the arithmetic of the Hessian, each axiom-free or depending on propext only. code/run_checks.sh runs them all. code/bllm/ holds the failure, change and retry record of the four targets on the Anaxia engine (release 3.0.5, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23469389).

items.summary: Sea level fingerprints connect the spatial distribution of rapid ice mass change to sea surface height (SSH) change, but the spatial resolving power of this inverse problem remains poorly quantified. Here we provide the first systematic, scale-resolved quantification of Greenland Ice Sheet mass change structure recoverable from its SSH fingerprint when ice loss geometry varies. We develop a physics-informed neural operator, constrained by an accurate neural-operator emulator of the forward sea level equation, to probe the information content of this ill-conditioned inverse problem. Across synthetic ice change ensembles, broad ice loss patterns can be recovered, but distinct ice fields can produce nearly identical fingerprints, so fine-scale structure depends on the assumed a-priori ice change distribution. Inversion fidelity varies with the wavelength and amplitude of ice mass change. An empirical error law separates these effects and defines a scale-dependent accuracy ceiling. For a satellite-altimetry-derived reference field, the estimated fingerprint-only ceiling is $R^2\sim0.79$ under the present SSH observation geometry and matched-prior assumption. The leading three principal components explain 99.76% of fingerprint variance, yet higher-order components retain information needed to distinguish finer ice change structure. SSH observations near Greenland carry most information on ice loss locations. Applying the leading fingerprint principal components to the observed 1993--2019 SSH rate recovers the large-scale Greenland fingerprint, while the residual field is correlated with basin-scale bathymetry, consistent with unresolved sterodynamic variability. These results establish a quantitative empirical bound on fingerprint-only ice-loss resolving power and identify how independent observations and ice sheet constraints can improve inference.
items.title: Neural Operators Reveal Scale-Dependent Limits on Recovering Greenland Ice Loss from Sea Level Fingerprints

items.summary: Abstract This integrative research synthesis develops a candidate relational architecture across quantum foundations, physical history, persistent organization, relational time, and the recovery problem for spacetime. Its method is unification by decomposition : constraint, weighting, singular factualization, and retention are treated as distinct operations with distinct evidential burdens. Key Analyses & Framework Quantum Foundations & Entanglement: The double slit separates coherent alternatives, receiver-defined effects, Born weighting, and the $n = 1$ record. The Sorkin hierarchy and reconstruction literature delimit what is already formally known and leave open the physical motivation for second-order weighting. Entanglement is analyzed through a missing-loss audit: spatial routing, operational differentiation, and dynamical decoupling do not by themselves demonstrate ontological severance of a nonfactorizable joint state. Ontology & Event-Factualization: Primitive factualization is treated as a technical event-ontology posit, with fundamental agency as a stronger interpretive hypothesis (alongside objective stochasticity, Bohmian completion, Everettian branching, and collapse dynamics as comparison classes). A present-state coherence veto prevents absolute factualization while coherence-bearing degrees of freedom remain causally accessible to future interactions in which their phase relation can again matter. Retained factual consequences provide the bridge to physical history, memory, differential persistence, and increasingly organized agency. Downstream Physics & Empirical Testing: Transition and stabilization are treated as relational roles of one field-energy reality rather than new substances. The synthesis incorporates a fully exposed prospective transition-stabilization kill test in a driven liquid-to-vapor system and preserves planetary, gravitational, and spacetime extensions as explicitly conditional research branches. Methodological Stance: No universal master equation is claimed. The program is a structured ontology, audit, and research architecture whose modules must earn mathematical or empirical closure independently. Philosophical Extensions (Dual-Aspect Hypothesis): A further dual-aspect factualist hypothesis, with a panexperiential extension, distinguishes the publicly accessible objective face of factual processes from a minimally subjective first-person-like aspect associated with irreducible factual resolution. This is presented as a stronger ontological interpretation, not as an experimentally established consequence. It does not identify an elementary subjective aspect with a subject, mind, or consciousness. Complex biological agency is treated as potentially nested and hierarchically integrated, while the combination of elementary subjective loci into a unified subject is left as an explicit unresolved problem.
items.title: Unification by Decomposition — A Relational Physical Architecture from Quantum Possibility to Factualization, Retained History, Stabilization, and Spacetime

items.summary: Where Yes and No Become Maybe The nested partner ring read as a folded square: a rolling stack, four providers, a straight-line gradient and a square-root address Driven by Dean A. Kulik  October 2026 Abstract The nested partner ring is Dean Kulik’s construction. Reverse a binary word, unless it is a palindrome, then complement it. Place the smaller member of every pair in ascending order on one half of a circle, set each partner directly opposite its word, and swap the two words that meet at the centre seam. items.summary: Conditional memory expands language-model capacity through selective lookup, but the full embedding table must remain available for every possible input. We introduce Conditional Program (CP), a compressed representation that reconstructs only the rows an input requests. CP represents each row by a short code and a local scale, with a reconstruction program shared across the table. We instantiate this representation with a Gaussian trellis, norm restoration and independently decodable row records. CP's two-bit code lowers output KL by 41--63\% relative to 2-bit round-to-nearest. Analysis across three trained n-gram memory families shows that Gaussian-like coordinate statistics coexist with learned relationships among rows; at matched storage budgets, the shared trellis outperforms the fitted codebooks and low-rank residual variants we test. For DeepSeek, it reduces table storage from 203GB to 51GB, leaving room for larger workloads when the table is kept on GPU.
items.title: N-Gram Memories at Two Bits: Quantizing Lookup Tables in Large Language Models

items.summary: How much classical information can a noisy optical channel carry when both signal energy and preshared entanglement are limited? This work gives an exact capacity frontier for this joint resource problem. It allows one to determine the best asymptotic communication rate, price the benefit of additional entanglement, and distinguish the effect of tolerating errors from that of changing how entanglement is supplied. Exact capacity under two resource constraints The setting is any fixed bosonic Gaussian channel \(\Phi\) with finitely many input and output modes. Signal energy is measured by a positive quadratic Hamiltonian \(H_G=\tfrac12 R^{\mathsf T}GR\), with \(G>0\) and ground energy \(E_0\); \(R\) collects the canonical quadratures. The budgets satisfy \(E\ge E_0\) and \(P\ge0\). For an \(n\)-use code, the mean total signal energy is at most \(nE\), while the same initially shared maximally entangled state has Schmidt rank \(K_n\) satisfying \(\log K_n\le nP\). Thus \(P\) is a strictly supplied entanglement rate. Encoders may be arbitrary joint quantum operations, and decoding may be collective. The classical capacity is \[ C(E,P)=\max_{\substack{U\ge V\;\mathrm{physical}\\ \frac12\operatorname{Tr}(GU)\le E,\;S_G(V)\le P}}\bigl[S_G(\Phi U)+S_G(V)-S_G(\Phi^c V)\bigr]. \] Here \(V\) is a Gaussian seed covariance, \(U\) is the average-input covariance, and \(U-V\) is the displacement-modulation covariance. A covariance is physical when \(V+i\Omega/2\ge0\), where \(\Omega\) is the canonical commutation matrix and the vacuum covariance is \(I/2\). The notation \(S_G\) denotes Gaussian von Neumann entropy, and \(\Phi^c\) is the full complementary channel, including any environment purification. All logarithms are natural, so rates are in nats per channel use. This formula replaces optimization over arbitrary quantum block codes by a finite-dimensional covariance optimization. It supplies both an achievable rate and a converse against non-Gaussian, correlated encodings. At \(P=0\), it also determines the unassisted capacity of general fixed finite-mode Gaussian channels, including channels without a passive decomposition into independent modes. The reduction specifies the exact capacity value; it does not require a closed-form optimizer for every device. Energy and strict entanglement supply respond differently to errors For a fixed allowed average error \(0\le\varepsilon<1\), the exact capacity under the mean-energy constraint is \[ C_\varepsilon(E,P)=C\!\left(E_0+\frac{E-E_0}{1-\varepsilon},\,P\right). \] Allowing failure rescales the mean energy above the ground state, but leaves the strict initial entanglement budget unchanged. The proof uses an exponential strong converse for codes whose inputs obey a hard total-energy cutoff. In a different model, where a readable flag permits random entanglement supply constrained only on average, the work establishes an achievable bound and a strict small-supply advantage for thermal attenuation at positive energy and fixed nonzero error. That comparison identifies the operational importance of the supply rule; it is not a complete capacity characterization of the flagged model. The communication value of entanglement For a thermal attenuator, let \(0<\eta<1\) be the transmissivity, \(b>0\) the output mean photon number for vacuum input, and \(N\) the input mean photon number. Write its capacity as \(C_N(P)\), and define \(g(N)=(N+1)\log(N+1)-N\log N\). The gain from entanglement obeys the sharp bound \[ 0\le C_N(P)-C_N(0)\le\frac{\eta}{1+b}\,P. \] For every fixed \(N>0\), the coefficient \(\eta/(1+b)\) is attained as the initial right derivative at \(P=0\). In the low-photon limit, the stronger resource law is \[ C_N(P)-C_N(0)=\frac{\eta}{1+b}\min\{P,g(N)\}+O(N),\qquad N\downarrow0. \] The remainder is uniform over \(P\ge0\) at fixed \(\eta\) and positive \(b\). Noise therefore determines the conversion efficiency, while \(g(N)\sim N\log(1/N)\) sets the entanglement scale
items.title: A universal energy–entanglement capacity frontier for Gaussian optical channels

items.summary: Anaxia, the BLLM engine, with the source, the Lean development and the checks of the paper BLLM: Beyond the LLM with Deep Human-Mind-AI by D. Bhattacharjee and U. Bhattacharya. The engine is the Python package eBLLM (command anaxia ), a Lean 4 library and the container image ghcr.io/creelie/bllm-engine, which carries no model weights. The paper proves, in a model with independent runs, that certifying self-modifications costs an entropy (the entropy law), that a sound infinite self-improvement of finite cost exists exactly when one series converges, that a proposer needs a number of proposals set by a Rényi entropy of order one half, and that n verified layers sharing one budget cost at least n log(n/θ). Sixty-five of its theorems are proved in Lean 4 with Mathlib, each depending only on the three standard axioms. The engine combines known constructions in a typed crossing network with a program check and a refuter for every candidate, a shared memory and five target agents, and builds new objects in construction mode: a goal-directed builder and an exists-forall search, each followed by an independent gate. From the rules of Steinberg's problem it rebuilds the gadgets of the 2016 counterexample of Cohen-Addad, Hebdige, Král', Li and Salgado; it finds nothing on Erdős's question for cycles of length 4 to 6. Layer towers of depth one to three, a ladder and a mesh, are compared with the crossing loop at the same number of checks. A Hodge-only run of twelve rounds leaves every target point at the same gap. None of the five benchmark problems (the lattice Yang–Mills mass gap, the Hodge conjecture, the standard conjecture of Lefschetz type, Chowla's conjecture, Erdős problem 1183) is solved. The registry of the systems, methods and collections the engine draws on, with what it takes from each and what it leaves, is src/ebllm/bllm/data/sources.json and Appendix D of the paper.

items.summary: LLM system capabilities depend not only on model parameters but also on the executable harnesses that organize information acquisition, tool use, reasoning, and memory. Recursive harness evolution can automate their design, but how it can reliably discover generalizable systems from limited, noisy, and repeatedly reused feedback remains unclear. We study this question in agentic video understanding, where rich multimodal evidence and coupled mechanisms make harness optimization challenging. We first introduce VHarness-BRSI, a recursive self-improvement framework that evolves video harnesses around a frozen vision-language model. Analyzing over 4,000 evolved candidates, we find it competitive with hand-engineered systems but identify three interconnected failure modes: validation overfitting, search-budget dilution, and the early-experience trap. We trace all three to a common root: the same imperfect validation evidence drives both harness revisions and the proposer's search strategy. We therefore propose VHarness-SRSI, an evidence-governed framework in which every search decision rests on evidence that is transferable, sufficient, and gathered before the search commits. It restricts the proposer to content-free feedback, informs exploration with instrumented warm-up experiments, and develops mechanisms in isolated probe-race branches before factorial composition and joint refinement. Across four video understanding benchmarks, VideoHarness-SRSI improves the equally weighted mean held-out score by 6.2% relative to VideoHarness-BRSI and reduces the mean validation-test gap by 37.9%. Reliable harness evolution thus depends on how search is organized and informed, not only on how well it optimizes validation performance.

items.summary: Code, independent checks and the record of the Anaxia engine for the paper Which String Vibrations Become Which Generations on the Dwork Quintic by Deep Bhattacharjee and Ushashi Bhattacharya. The paper determines, for the heterotic string with the standard embedding on the one-parameter family of quintic threefolds, which vibration modes become which families of charged particles. The 101 families are labelled by 101 distinct characters of the symmetry group (Z/5)^3, and the 24 characters that do not occur are the classes of the permutations of (0,1,2,3,4). Every Yukawa coupling allowed by the symmetry is a power of the modulus, psi^r with r = 0, 1, 2, 3 on 566, 425, 280 and 160 unordered triples, and every other coupling vanishes. The invariant deformation pairs each family with exactly one partner, so that the mass matrix has determinant psi^70, full rank away from the Fermat point and rank 51 there, where the masses are given in closed form by the Gamma function. The Geometric Selection Conjecture is shown to be equivalent to the existence of one viable vacuum fixed by mirror symmetry, and no smooth quintic and no free quotient of one carries three families. The existence of a viable vacuum is open. The archive holds 64 independent checks: a C program for the labels, the couplings allowed by the group and the mass map, a C++ expansion of the Hessian over its 120 permutations, Python checks of the socle, the Hessian, the intersection form of the Fermat quintic and the Gamma values, a Julia check of the Hodge norms, a Macaulay2 computation of the Jacobian ring at two rational values of the modulus with the socle functional on all 3876 monomials of degree fifteen, and 11 Lean 4 theorems on the counts and the arithmetic of the Hessian, each axiom-free or depending on propext only. code/run_checks.sh runs them all. code/bllm/ holds the failure, change and retry record of the four targets on the Anaxia engine (release 3.0.5, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23469389).

items.summary: Which biological findings enter a reported explanation depends on how the model population was constructed, a choice predictive validation alone does not reveal. We fitted 10,000 L2-regularised logistic regression models to TCGA pan-cancer tumour-versus-normal data: 100 regularisation strengths on 100 train-test splits, with patients fixed within each split. Strongly and weakly regularised models differ in mean accuracy by only 0.21 percentage points, yet prioritise different genes systematically with regularisation strength. Averaging explanations across a hyperparameter grid produces a top-50 panel sharing 41 genes with a single fitted model, but which model depends on the grid centre (Spearman correlation 0.92, 350 simulated practitioners). For 43 of 50 practitioners, the panel combines genes from strongly and weakly regularised models more fully than any fitted model: the explanation belongs to no model whose accuracy was established. A conventional grid recovers only a quarter of genes favoured exclusively by the strongest regularisation. HMGCS2 ranks among the top 50 in 73 of 100 strongly regularised fits and no weakly regularised fits, yet appears in none of 50 simulated reports. Reconstructing a published biomarker workflow on 20 cohort resamples reveals a different failure: the closest refit contains only 23 of the averaged panel's 50 genes, and no panel gene appears in all 20 refits. We define model-relative provenance as how much of a panel any single fitted model contains, distinct from workflow provenance recording how an analysis was run. We provide measurements to make the model population, the choice that selects from it, and that provenance reportable.
items.title: Same Accuracy, Different Gene Panels: How the Hyperparameter Grid Chooses the Reported Explanation

items.summary: Assembly traces can support explicit probabilistic inference without being treated as recovered program meaning. Active Assembly Theory and Practice makes that distinction executable: transparent x86-64 fixtures are decoded with Capstone, traced under bounded Unicorn emulation, and mapped to typed observations that distinguish missing, unseen, and unsupported evidence. Two Generalized Notation Notation (GNN) specifications define passive-phase and prospective sensor models whose tensors drive real pymdp execution. A native categorical Julia/RxInfer companion consumes the passive model's same parameters (Friedman 2026; Heins et al. 2022; Bagaev et al. 2023). The sensor Agent selects an action before fixture evidence is acquired. Independent finite calculations check beliefs and policy scores; native smoothing uses the same parameters and first-observation convention. Every inference comparator and fitted diagnostic also consumes an upstream-parsed numeric GNN specification, with source-bound runtime instances and rendered model graphs. A corpus of 10 authored fixtures supports complete-fixture exclusion diagnostics. At the fixed informative likelihood, the memoryless decoder outperforms the temporal filter; temporal advantages appear under synthetic observation ambiguity. Designed category ambiguity remains a visible failure case. The separate Gaussian and categorical Bethe free-energy diagnostics are not compared numerically with policy expected free energy. The quotient benchmark contains 64 transformation-family identifiers and 4096 rows, with 16 families held out from model fitting. The co-primary portfolio includes an interpretable classifier, a temporal probabilistic model, a fixed one-layer tanh recurrent classifier, and surface baselines; the temporal endpoint reaches balanced accuracy 0.775 and macro-F1 0.772 on this frozen bounded benchmark. Held-out identifiers share authored template lineages with the fitting data. Family-resampling intervals and conditional randomization diagnostics therefore describe this finite inventory; the retrospective protocol correction withholds superiority claims. A complementary pinned static-only corpus supplies 5 licensed source projects and 100 source-contract rows, including 40 lexical witnesses, 40 contract-directed near misses, and 20 identity controls. The corpus establishes provenance and coverage; it does not execute arbitrary external binaries or support application-effectiveness claims. Selected normalized machine-state relations are checked by Python, native execution, and a bounded Lean fragment. Exact finite sensing certificates and source-bound reader artifacts make assumptions and failures inspectable. Independent physical replication remains unearned. The contribution is a reproducible substrate for testing assembly-to-inference mechanisms, with explicit limits on semantics, statistical generalization, and external validity.

items.summary: Anaxia, the BLLM engine, with the source, the Lean development and the checks of the paper BLLM: Beyond the LLM with Deep Human-Mind-AI by D. Bhattacharjee and U. Bhattacharya. The engine is the Python package eBLLM (command anaxia ), a Lean 4 library and the container image ghcr.io/creelie/bllm-engine, which carries no model weights. The paper proves, in a model with independent runs, that certifying self-modifications costs an entropy (the entropy law), that a sound infinite self-improvement of finite cost exists exactly when one series converges, that a proposer needs a number of proposals set by a Rényi entropy of order one half, and that n verified layers sharing one budget cost at least n log(n/θ). Sixty-five of its theorems are proved in Lean 4 with Mathlib, each depending only on the three standard axioms. The engine combines known constructions in a typed crossing network with a program check and a refuter for every candidate, a shared memory and five target agents, and builds new objects in construction mode: a goal-directed builder and an exists-forall search, each followed by an independent gate. From the rules of Steinberg's problem it rebuilds the gadgets of the 2016 counterexample of Cohen-Addad, Hebdige, Král', Li and Salgado; it finds nothing on Erdős's question for cycles of length 4 to 6. Layer towers of depth one to three, a ladder and a mesh, are compared with the crossing loop at the same number of checks. A Hodge-only run of twelve rounds leaves every target point at the same gap. None of the five benchmark problems (the lattice Yang–Mills mass gap, the Hodge conjecture, the standard conjecture of Lefschetz type, Chowla's conjecture, Erdős problem 1183) is solved. The registry of the systems, methods and collections the engine draws on, with what it takes from each and what it leaves, is src/ebllm/bllm/data/sources.json and Appendix D of the paper.
items.title: BLLM: Beyond the LLM with Deep Human-Mind-AI

items.summary: annotations4all is a schema-first Python library for LLM-assisted span annotation, including named entity recognition. Users define their own tag schemas; the library generates chat prompts, parses annotated model responses and maps annotations to character offsets in the original text. The library keeps annotation mechanics separate from research workflows: it bundles no corpus or fixed ontology, performs no evaluation, and does not promise model quality. Provider support uses explicit OpenAI-compatible routes rather than native SDKs. What the library provides Schema-first prompt generation and response parsing. Configurable taggers, German and English prompt templates, metadata-bearing spans and structured parser warnings. Per-label annotation and deterministic merge. Independent label runs can be combined using containment-derived hierarchy, explicit conflict reports and bounded anchoring. One request per run has a corresponding inference cost; merge is not a semantic error repair. Provider policies and capability evidence. A generic OpenAI-compatible client, provider-policy clients, explicit reasoning activation and effort, request limits, packaged hints and offline capability reports. Remote verification requires opt-in; metadata does not prove account access or successful inference. Optional read-only terminal viewer. Browse saved annotations, inspect nested spans and compare two sources using synchronized split or compact diff views. The viewer does not modify annotation files or run inference. Release notes 0.3.0 Provider-policy clients and automatic selection for documented endpoint routes; separate reasoning activation and effort, validated request conflicts, and configurable request limits. Capability reporting and packaged provider/model hints with explicit evidence boundaries. Optional Textual viewer with disjoint source selection, semantic gold-layer deduplication, split/diff views, mouse navigation, responsive legends and local diff inspection. Data-dependent contrast optimization in an isolated subprocess, opaque light/dark themes and persistent theme selection with conflict-safe settings. Deprecation warnings on construction of the old native llama.cpp and Ollama wrappers, for removal in 0.4.0. Public provider-policy clients are not deprecated. items.summary: In autonomous driving, perceiving surrounding objects is not enough: failing to understand how they move and interact over time can lead to dangerous decisions. Evaluating vision-language models (VLMs) therefore requires testing whether they connect past spatial observations to future consequences. Yet existing benchmarks often assess edge cases through basic perception questions or test temporal understanding in simple scenarios, leaving complex spatiotemporal reasoning underexplored. We introduce STRIDE (SpatioTemporal Reasoning In Driving Edge Cases), an object-centric benchmark for long-tail, safety-critical driving scenarios. STRIDE covers six task families: spatial perception, spatial understanding, temporal memory, temporal extrapolation, trajectory prediction, and scene-context awareness. It pairs multiple-choice questions probing individual spatiotemporal judgments with related free-form visual question answering (VQA) requiring detailed scene explanations and justifications of driving decisions. We prioritize scenes with unusual object behaviors and complex traffic interactions, generate reference answers from structured dataset annotations through automated procedures, and use limited language-model assistance and human verification to ensure annotation quality. Across 12 proprietary, open-weight, and driving-specialized models, even the best performer, GPT-6-Astra, achieves only 43.4% average multiple-choice accuracy, versus an approximately 20% random-choice baseline. Further analysis reveals that strong performance in describing driving scenes does not necessarily translate to accurate safety-critical judgments, and that models struggle more with reconstructing object motion than recalling past positions. STRIDE thus exposes spatiotemporal driving limitations that aggregate VQA scores can conceal.
items.title: STRIDE: Evaluating Spatiotemporal Reasoning in Driving Edge Cases

items.summary: This archive accompanies the article "A Reproducible Webots-Based Benchmarking Framework for UAV Mobility Modeling: Comparative Evaluation of Random Waypoint and Gauss-Markov Trajectories in Urban and Open-Terrain Environments" (Journal of Engineering, University of Baghdad). items.summary: This repository provides the reproducible analysis materials accompanying the research article “Bitcoin and Sovereign Reserve Management: Portfolio Allocation, Model Sensitivity, and Downside Risk.” The study examines the sensitivity of Bitcoin allocations within a sovereign reserve-related portfolio framework, with particular emphasis on measurement consistency, model specification, allocation stability and downside risk. The empirical framework combines U.S. official reserve positions, Treasury gold holdings valued at market prices, and Bitcoin market-price observations. The principal estimation period covers April 2016 to July 2026, comprising 124 consecutive monthly changes. An extended historical sample beginning in January 2013 is used for sensitivity analysis. The analysis applies a Black–Litterman allocation framework with explicit budget constraints and alternative portfolio specifications. The reproducibility framework covers baseline portfolio estimation, alternative Bitcoin views and confidence levels, long-only allocation constraints, covariance sensitivity, rolling-window estimation, joint stationary bootstrap resampling and historical and hypothetical stress scenarios. Risk analysis includes volatility, Value at Risk (VaR95) and Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR95), with particular attention to adverse Bitcoin market conditions. The associated materials document the empirical procedures used to examine the sensitivity of estimated Bitcoin weights to data construction, estimation windows, covariance assumptions and portfolio constraints. They support independent examination of the quantitative results, robustness analyses, tables and figures reported in the accompanying research. The study uses publicly available financial and institutional data from the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, U.S. Treasury Fiscal Data, the World Bank and Coin Metrics. Associated research article: Bitcoin and Sovereign Reserve Management: Portfolio Allocation, Model Sensitivity, and Downside Risk. Research area: Financial Economics, Sovereign Reserve Management, Portfolio Optimization and Cryptocurrency Risk.
items.title: Bitcoin and Sovereign Reserve Management: Reproducible Analysis and Replication Package

items.summary: AI agents increasingly use files and software tools to produce professional deliverables. Such work draws on materials, decisions, and feedback accumulated across assignments. We introduce OfficeTown, a generative simulation framework for professional organizations in which tasks and their context arise from continuing organizational work. From a natural-language description of an organization's purpose and activities, OfficeTown initializes an organization whose members coordinate work, delegate bounded assignments to assistant agents, and review their deliverables. Artifacts, decisions, and unresolved matters persist and shape subsequent work, while responsibilities and permissions determine what each member can see and do. We curate work requests, their context, and review feedback into executable resources for evaluation and learning. We construct OfficeTown Bench with 406 tasks and 4,836 evaluation criteria from 23 simulated organizations across eight professional domains, incorporating domain-expert feedback. Frontier-model evaluations reveal substantial remaining headroom. Supervised fine-tuning and on-policy distillation on OfficeTown data substantially improve Qwen3.5-9B on external professional-work benchmarks, including GDPval. Supplementary evaluations show that the principal--assistant harness achieves higher scores than the single- and multi-agent baselines tested. These results highlight the value of organizational simulation in generating work-grounded data and environments for the continued development of generalist agents.
items.title: OfficeTown: Generative Organizations for Evolving Agent Intelligence

items.summary: LLM-agent memory selection often uses retrieval rankings based on record relevance or individual influence. Such rankings cannot identify sufficient subsets under redundant or jointly necessary evidence. We study per-decision memory sufficiency: selecting a small subset that preserves full-memory behavior. To separate search error from model error, we introduce JointCoreBench, a benchmark with nine interaction families, six workflow domains, natural-language decisions, and exact sufficient-set oracles, and JointCore, a relevance cost-ordered group-deletion baseline that tests blocks before individual records. On 6,912 exact conditions, cost-ordered JointCore recovers a minimum-cost sufficient set in 100.0% of cases, reduces subset evaluations from 30.00 to 11.13 (62.9%), and achieves 87.8% active-memory savings. Across four 12B-70B model families and 432 tasks per model, its unweighted mean is 10.28 versus 16.00 model queries and 50.6% versus 43.1% minimum-cost recovery relative to cost aware singleton deletion. Both methods preserve full-memory behavior under the deterministic primary interface. Tests with physical deletion, UNKNOWN masks, PENDING sentinels, counterfactual values, and alternative labels identify interface dependent behavior. JointCore is an efficient benchmark baseline; the study does not establish deployment-ready memory compression.
items.title: Beyond Marginal Influence: Interaction-Aware Memory Selection for LLM Agents
